title: A Drill About Childhood in Persia

content.text: ## Alchemorph x KeOSz x Mtwn x Jaya Prime - A Drill About Childhood in Persia Back in 2013, in May, this whole thing kicked off as a simple mashup ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gtN1D4TA_fE))... Alchemorph Soundtracks colliding with KeOSz and Mtwn. Fast forward thirteen years, and we've evolved that raw concept into a proper, full-blooded collaboration. Alchemorph goes way back to the wild west of the creative commons -- that golden Web 2.0 era of internet music. As a longtime fan, I knew exactly what I wanted to do: take their sweet, lullaby-like instrumentation and crash it head-on into heavy drill and bass elements, weaving in my own instrumental touches. I layered in some extra effects, completely re-orchestrated a few cello sections, and then... yanked a haunting choir straight out of another track I'm currently cooking up. As I write this, I can't say much about the project codenamed "Pigeonblade"... but know there's a lot more coming down the pipe. I'd somehow formed this wildly incorrect opinion that DnB, jungle, and drill were dead genres. But even in my short time down in Costa Rica, I've seen some serious die-hards still living, breathing, and spreading the music. I already knew Europe was holding the line -- especially Spain and Germany -- but seeing it out here gave me the spark to start building on that old project again. This? This is just a small glimpse of things to come. \[[Video on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UdUc1AkdLDY)\] \[[Alchemorph on Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/artist/7EE7umf0SzN7Sy8erv47K1?si=mGdO3AeVRGqxpzMc9M_m2Q)\] \[[KeOSz on Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4lFmHaaR3XATl9yVLqWuhz?si=grNJXwHRTTaKteJ1jJx2lQ)\] \[[Mtwn on Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/artist/3whG4tgVMNOE7SSAdl0GhK?si=XVlLKLXMQ8Wp42aOnAG75g)\] Note: The video was generated with Gemini Veo 3.1. It's entirely AI-driven up until the 4:11 mark, where my new art for the upcoming 20-year anniversary edition of my award-winning _Synapse Collapse_ closes it out. So, to anyone out there rallying against the robot uprising... this is your chance to tap out, fleshie.

## On Doves, Pigeons, and Persia

While pigeons were used as far back as Ancient Egypt to communicate, it was the Persians who elevated the practice to an entirely new art form. Under King Cyrus the Great, they trained high-speed homing pigeons that flew faster -- and with more dauntless discipline -- than any bird before them. They built a massive relay network between the capital and Assyria... warning of potential attacks, organizing troop movements, and effectively inventing one of the earliest forms of long-distance military communication.

The enemies of Persia were completely clueless. They assumed the great empire's sorcerers had thwarted their attacks with dark magic... when in reality, it was a bird. Just a bird. They flew faster than horses and lived in the pockets of the masters they served. It was just one of many advantages Ancient Persia had over its enemies, but it remains one of their longest-lasting legacies, later hijacked by countless other states and empires.

Now here's the kicker: a dove has zero biological differences from a pigeon.

They're classified as the exact same bird. Yet somehow, in the "modern world" we currently reside in, this incredible creature -- the pigeon -- has become a universal symbol of "trash" and "refuse." Meanwhile, a mere change in color -- the dove -- gets paraded around the globe as the ultimate symbol of "peace."

_I call it lunacy._

You'll find me spending almost as much time with pigeons as I do with my brothers and sisters that others call "black birds" -- lifetime compatriots of mine from an early age.

And if you've enjoyed the song itself, then it's yours, Love. Take it with you. May it grant you wings in the dark of night.
